The height, *h *cm, of each of 120 plants is measured.
 The cumulative frequency diagram shows this information.

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4a](assets/007-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4a.png)

Use the cumulative frequency diagram to find an estimate of

i) the median,

............................................ cm [1]

ii) the interquartile range,

............................................ cm [2]

iii) the 60<sup>th</sup> percentile,

............................................ cm [1]

iv) the number of plants with a height greater than 40cm.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *There are a total of 120 plants, so an estimate of the median will be the 60*<sup>*th*</sup>* (120 ÷ 2) plant. *
*Use a ruler to draw a horizontal line from 60 on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then draw a vertical line down to the height axis. *

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4ai-working](assets/008-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4ai-working.png)

> *Read off the height axis to estimate the median.*

**Median = 25 cm**<sup>**  **</sup>**[1]**

ii) *The interquartile range (IQR) is equal to the upper quartile (UQ) subtract the lower quartile (LQ). *
*For the LQ, use a ruler to draw horizontal lines from 30 (one-quarter of 120) on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then draw a vertical line down to the height axis. *
*For the UQ, use a ruler to draw horizontal lines from 90 (three-quarters of 120) on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then draw a vertical line down to the height axis.*

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aii-working](assets/009-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aii-working.png)

> *Read off the height axis to find the LQ and UQ.*

*LQ = 22 * 
*UQ = 32 *

**Either correct ****[1]**

> *Calculate the IQR by subtracting the LQ from the UQ.*

*IQR = 32 - 22 = 10*

**IQR = 10 cm**<sup>** **</sup>**[1]**

iii) *The 60*<sup>*th*</sup>* percentile will be 60% of the way through the data.*

`60 percent sign space of space 120 space equals 60 over 100 space cross times space 120 space equals space 72`

> *i.e. The 60*<sup>*th*</sup>* percentile will be the 72*<sup>*nd*</sup>* value.*

> *Find the value of the 60*<sup>*th*</sup>* percentile by using a ruler to draw a horizontal line from 72 on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then draw a vertical line down to the height axis. *

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aiii-working](assets/010-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aiii-working.png)

> *Read off the height axis to find the 60*<sup>*th*</sup>* percentile.*

**60**<sup>**th**</sup>** percentile = 27 cm**<sup>** **</sup>**[1]**

iv) *Find the cumulative frequency at a height of 40 cm by using a ruler to draw a vertical line from 40 on the height axis to the curve; then draw a horizontal line across to the cumulative frequency axis.*

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aiv-working](assets/011-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q4aiv-working.png)

> *Read off the cumulative frequency axis - beware, this is not the final answer!*

*114 plants have a height of ****less**** than 40 cm*

**[1]**

> *We require the number of plants with a height greater than 40 cm so subtract 114 from the total number of plants (120).*

*120 - 114 = 6*

**Approximately 6 plants have a height greater than 40 cm ****[1]**
